intent: One dark, monochrome, native text field. The label rests inside the field and, once focused or filled, rises onto the top hairline while the border opens a notch around it. Validation is a prop: when a validate function is supplied, invalid values show error copy after they rest, and valid values show success copy and a drawn tick. Built with React 19, Tailwind CSS v4 and motion/react, with lucide-react for the mail glyph in the demo.

stack.styling: Tailwind CSS v4 (@container on the root, arbitrary values) plus one ifl- namespaced style block for the notch mask, focus border, autofill and disabled rules
stack.animation: motion/react (animate for the notch edges, the label's clip width and the tweened count; motion values for the label; AnimatePresence mode popLayout for messages and the count; pathLength for the tick). The field has no entrance of its own; the demo stage reveals it
stack.icons: lucide-react Mail, 16px, stroke 1.6, supplied as the prefix in the demo

layout.root: @container block, max-width 420px, full width below; the field and the helper row sit in a body wrapper that carries the disabled dim
layout.field: 56px tall (md) or 64px (lg), border-radius 12px, position relative; surface layer, masked border layer, label, prefix slot, input, trailing slot, stacked in that order
layout.padding: 16px horizontal (md), 18px (lg). The prefix and trailing slots are measured with ResizeObserver; the label, notch start and input padding add their measured width plus a 10px gap
layout.trailingSlot: holds the suffix and, beside it, the success tick, at a 10px gap; its measured width sets the input's right padding
layout.helperRow: flex, items start, gap 16px; message left (min-width 0, flex 1), count right and shrink-0; both inset by the field padding. The count reserves its width while hidden so the message never reflows
layout.collapse: the label and text keep their offsets at every width. Below a 300px field (a sidebar, or a 320px phone with page padding) the side padding tightens by 4px and the resting label steps down 1px; the helper row gap is 12px below the @xs container width and 16px above

typography.input: sans, 16px (md) or 18px (lg), so iOS does not zoom
typography.label: sans, 15px (md) or 17px (lg), 14px/16px in a narrow field, line box 20px; floated state is the same element scaled to 0.76 from the left centre. At rest the max width is the field minus the label offset and trailing inset, with an ellipsis. Floated, the clip width tweens to that run divided by 0.76 (capped 8px short of the corner), so the scaled label uses the full hairline up to the trailing slot and never overshoots it mid-rise. The notch is sized from an unclipped, invisible twin of the label
typography.message: sans 13px, leading 1.45; 13.5px from the @sm container breakpoint
typography.counter: mono 12px, tabular-nums, written 33 / 40 with thin spaces (U+2009) around the slash; digits tween over 180ms

color.usage: error colours only on the border, the message, the label (full strength while focused, 80% at rest) and the count at the limit; success colours only on the border, the message and the tick; the count is muted from 80% of the limit, full ink for the last three characters; everything else monochrome

border.rest: 1px inset box-shadow at the hairline colour
border.hover: 1px at the hover hairline, on pointer devices only (@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine))
border.focusWithin: 1.5px at the focus hairline, on the masked border so the line opens around the label; on an error or success field, 2px in that state colour, declared after the state rules so focus wins
border.error: 1.5px at the error colour (2px while focused)
border.success: 1.5px at the success colour (2px while focused)
border.outline: none; there is no outer focus ring, so the notch is never crossed by a second line

motion.rise: label y and scale and notch edges share 320ms ease-out [0.22, 1, 0.36, 1]; notch edges write --ifl-nl and --ifl-nr imperatively from animate onUpdate, interruptible from the current position
motion.messages: popLayout cross-fade: enter from y 6px and blur 3px, exit to y -6px and blur 3px, 260ms ease-out
motion.count: rises like a message when it appears; digits tween to the new value over 180ms
motion.tick: scale 0.8 to 1 with opacity over 240ms; path pathLength 0 to 1 over 420ms, 100ms delay
motion.reveal: none on the field: a form primitive is visible the moment it mounts. The demo stage fades the field in once (10px rise, 6px blur, 600ms)
motion.autofill: a :-webkit-autofill rule plays the ifl-autofill keyframes; onAnimationStart reads the DOM value and marks the field as filled so the label stays floated
motion.reducedMotion: no transforms, offsets or blur on the label, notch, messages, count or tick; colour and opacity changes at 150ms or less; notch set instantly; tick drawn complete

validation.validate: a function (value) => boolean passed by the host. Without it there is no error and no success tick
validation.idle: reward early, punish late: an invalid value is called out only after 800ms of rest, or when the field is left. Once called out, the error stays while the value is still wrong and goes straight to success when it is fixed, with no helper in between. Emptying the field, or making it valid, resets this, so the next mistake waits for a pause again. A forced error state counts as called out
validation.valid: a valid value clears the error straight away and shows the success text and tick
validation.demo: the demo passes an email check: local part, @, domain and a top-level domain of two or more letters

counter.appears: only once the value reaches 80% of maxLength; at rest with no value near the limit, nothing shows
counter.limit: the count reads muted, steps up to full ink for the last three characters and turns to the error colour at maxLength; the input stops there
counter.demo: maxLength 40, so the count appears at 32 characters; the Value control seeds a 33-character valid address, and the State control fills the field to match each forced state (ana.lumen@ for error, ana.lumen@studio.co for success, a filled field for disabled)

responsive.all: fluid to 420px; the field and helper row share one container; touch targets stay the full field height (56px or 64px)
responsive.widths: designed at 320, 390, 768 and 1440px; the label, notch, slots and count never overflow the field
responsive.touch: the whole field is the hit target, not the label; tapping the label focuses the input

accessibility: native input that takes type, name, autoComplete, inputMode, required, spellCheck and any other input attribute as passed
label associated with htmlFor; the label is pointer-events none so taps reach the input
onFocus, onBlur and onChange composed with the internal handlers; value and onValueChange work as a controlled pair
aria-invalid true in the error state; aria-describedby lists the suffix (when there is one), then the message container, then any host ids, so 'Optional' or a unit is heard with the field
message container aria-live polite, so the error and success copy is announced once per change
disabled uses the native disabled attribute and dims the body to 42% opacity with cursor not-allowed; the wrapper carries aria-disabled
decorative layers, the prefix glyph, the label twin and the trailing slot (suffix and tick) are aria-hidden; the suffix still reaches assistive technology through aria-describedby

focus is shown on the border as a 1.5px line at 0.90 ink (2px in the state colour for error and success); the field is keyboard operable with no extra ring, and an errored label stays full strength while focused

content.label: Work email (a long label ends in an ellipsis before the trailing slot)
content.helper: We’ll send receipts and invoices here.
content.count: hidden at rest, then 32 / 40 (thin spaces) from 80% of a 40-character limit

avoid: a filled background behind the label, or a Material-style underline field
a glow, gradient or coloured fill on focus
an outer focus ring or halo that runs over the notch
a red warning triangle or a shake animation on error
the label jumping between positions instead of rising along one path
a count before 80% of the limit, or a permanent 'Max N' label
a success tick that fades in rather than drawing
layout shift when the message changes, the label rises or the count appears
blur or opacity on the input text itself
emoji or decorative sparkles anywhere in the field
per-frame React state for the notch edges
the error dropping back to the helper on every keystroke while the user fixes it
an entrance animation on the field itself
